faults.fault: the explanation skipping the causal step
faults.finding: 'it sets how tall the peak is, V ÷ R, and so how sharply the current rises to it' does not say why a taller peak is a sharper one: far from f₀ the net reactance, which R does not touch, sets the current, so a smaller R raises only the top.
faults.fix: Say that away from f₀ the net reactance dominates Z whatever R is, so the flanks barely change and a smaller R lifts only the top, making the peak taller and narrower.

faults.fault: the explanation skipping the causal step
faults.finding: Q = X_L ÷ R is stated, not shown: the step that the supply's voltage at resonance is the resistor's, I × R, so the current cancels from (I × X_L) ÷ (I × R), is missing.
faults.fix: Add that at resonance the supply's voltage equals the resistor's, I × R, while the coil's is I × X_L, so their ratio is X_L ÷ R.

faults.fault: false absolute / a claim that fails in the real world
faults.finding: 'the capacitor's still stands a little above the supply's at every setting below 70 Hz' is 'a little' only far out (10.4 V at 10 Hz); at 45 Hz it is 38.2 V. At 70 Hz it equals the supply exactly.
faults.fix: Say it stays above the supply's at every setting below 70 Hz, only just at 10 Hz, and the coil's at every setting above 35 Hz.

faults.finding: 'half your pushes fight it' is a made-up fraction.
faults.fix: 'some of your pushes land against it'.

faults.finding: 'the first few cycles after switching on' understates it: with Q = 10 the build-up lasts many cycles.
faults.fix: 'the build-up after switching on is left out'.

faults.fault: unreadable picture / one name for each thing
faults.finding: The arrows are reactance arrows in ohms, yet screen 7 speaks of '50 V up and 50 V down' arrows without saying they have turned into volts.
faults.fix: Say screen 7 multiplies every arrow by the 5 A current, turning ohms into volts, the reverse of lesson 6's step.

faults.finding: Source 17 (230 V) is cited only in the numbers list, not in the words.
faults.fix: Add screen 11's mains circuit to practice's safety step with [^17]: 23 A and 460 V across the coil on a 230 V supply.

faults.fault: a claim that fails in the real world
faults.finding: 'would fail' is too certain of an overstressed part.
